serviceSummary: A local municipal cadastral custodian is evidenced by the official Dirección de Catastro Municipal lookup, while the state GeoWeb/GeoServer provides public GIS infrastructure. No verified urban parcel geometry was admitted.
queryOutcomes: English first-party discovery found the municipal Treasury lookup, state GeoWeb and official WMS catalog.
Spanish first-party discovery found the same local cadastral lookup and official Chiapas map/administrative references.
The municipal host timed out twice; no login, CAPTCHA bypass, unsafe lookup, or owner/address request was attempted.
requestOutcomes: GeoWeb HTML: HTTP 200; current JS references inspected.
GeoServer WMS GetCapabilities: HTTP 200; CRS and layer catalog inspected.
WFS parcelas bounded query: HTTP 200, zero features.
WFS RAN parcel-zone bounded query: HTTP 200, one MultiPolygon outside the target urban extent; not retained.
scopeLimits: The exact WUP point [14.89697903262, -92.268743483956] was preserved and not moved to force a hit.
A zero exact/bounded response is not treated as citywide absence.
State thematic layers and RAN zone parcels are not assumed to be Tapachula municipal cadastral coverage.
No raw source attribute set, owner data, address, titleholder, tax/account detail, or contact data was retained.
identityAndMapping: No retained GeoJSON sample. The RAN response exposed nuc_poligo as the apparent native polygon key; this remains unqualified because the feature was outside the target urban extent. Source-specific field mapping is documented in the city record only.
uncertainty: The municipal portal's underlying service contract and any urban cadastral geometry remain unverified due to timeout and the portal's tax-account scope. Public GeoServer presence does not prove citywide or municipal parcel coverage.
